quote: Regulatory flood protection elevation means the "base flood elevation" plus the "freeboard". In "special flood hazard areas" where base flood elevations (BFEs) have been determined, this elevation shall be the BFE plus one foot of freeboard. In "special flood hazard areas" where no BFE has been established, this elevation shall be at least two feet above the highest adjacent grade.

other_height_rules: Town brochure: all construction, in any zone, must meet V-zone elevation rules, i.e. bottom of lowest horizontal structural member at BFE + 2 ft (so the finished floor in A zones sits above BFE + 2 ft by the floor-system depth); no obstructions or utilities below that level. Building height is measured from the design flood elevation (BFE + 2 ft). The 2014 staff proposal also listed a minimum 8 ft clearance between lowest horizontal structural member and grade in A/V zones; I did not confirm it was adopted.
quote: Holden Beach requires all construction, regardless of where it occurs, to meet V-Zone construction elevation requirements. This means all new and substantially improved buildings must be built with two foot of freeboard calculated from the lowest horizontal structural member.
date_quote: January 12, 2015 ... New Building Height Ordinance The Town of Holden Beach is proposing changing the way the 35′ building height limit is measured and adding two feet of freeboard. ... Bottom line is if we don’t implement freeboard everyone’s insurance rates will go up ... PUBLIC HEARING ON THIS MATTER: 6:45 P. M. ON TUESDAY, JANUARY 13, 2015.
notes: Freeboard (2 ft) was added by Ordinance 15-01 (amending Ch. 154 Flood Damage Prevention and Ch. 157 Zoning), public hearing/vote 13 Jan 2015. Evidence the vote passed: HBPOA 'Very Large Structures' report (2015) cites 'Ordinance 15-01, which amends Chapter 154 Flood Damage Prevention and Chapter 157 Zoning Code' with 'DFE is Base flood Elevation plus 2’ freeboard'; HBPOA post 2015-08-17: 'The new code measures 31’ from the flood zone elevation plus two feet of “freeboard”.' Before: the town planning director's Dec 2014 NFIP presentation lists Holden Beach freeboard 'n/a' (others listed with 1-3 ft), so 0 ft locally before 2015. Ordinance 15-01 PDF (old hbtownhall.com URL) is dead and American Legal (codelibrary.amlegal.com, Ch. 154) returned 403/Cloudflare, so I could not quote the codified RFPE text directly; a search-engine snippet of § 154 reads 'BFE plus 2 feet of freeboard'. Current value from the town CRS brochure (PDF created 2023-06-19). Exact effective date of 15-01 (adoption vs later) not verified; 2015 used.
